complete_source_units.text: And judicial cases from other cities came to them.

These men saw a woman lovely in appearance, the wife of their brother from the sons of Israel, named Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah and wife of Joachim, walking in her husband’s garden in the evening. They desired her
and distorted their minds, turning their eyes aside so as not to look toward heaven or remember righteous judgments.
Both were stricken with desire for her, but neither admitted to the other the evil that possessed them concerning her. The woman herself knew nothing of this matter.
As dawn came, they would come, trying to outwit one another in their hurry to see who would appear to her first and speak with her.

And behold, she was walking as usual. One of the elders had arrived, and behold, the other came. One questioned the other, saying, “Why did you go out so early without taking me?” Then each confessed his anguish to the other.
One said to the other, “Let us go to her.” Having agreed, they approached her and tried to force her.
The Jewish woman said to them, “I know that if I do this, it means death for me; and if I do not, I will not escape your hands.
But it is better for me to fall into your hands without having done it than to sin before the Lord.”

The lawless men went back, making threats among themselves and plotting to kill her. They came to the assembly of the city where they were residing, and all the sons of Israel who were there sat together in council.
The two elders and judges stood up and said, “Send for Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah, who is Joachim’s wife.” They summoned her at once.
The woman arrived with her father and mother. Her male and female servants, numbering five hundred, also arrived, together with Susanna’s four children.
The woman was very delicate.
The lawless men ordered her to be uncovered, so that they might satisfy their desire for her beauty.
All her people, and everyone who knew her, wept.
The elders and judges stood up and laid their hands on her head.
But her heart trusted in the Lord her God. Raising her head, she wept within herself, saying,
“Lord, everlasting God, who knowest all things before they come into being, Thou knowest that I have not done what these lawless men wickedly allege against me.” And the Lord heard her petition.
The two elders said, “We were walking in her husband’s garden,
and as we went around the course, we saw this woman reclining with a man. We stood and watched them being intimate with one another,
and they did not know that we were standing there. Then we said to one another, ‘Let us find out who these people are.’
We approached and recognized her, but the young man fled, covered up.
We seized her and asked her, ‘Who is the man?’
She did not tell us who he was. We testify to these things.” The whole assembly believed them because they were elders and judges of the people.
And behold, an angel of the Lord was there as she was being led out to perish. As he had been commanded, the angel gave a spirit of understanding to Daniel, who was young.
Daniel parted the crowd, stood in their midst, and said, “Are you so foolish, sons of Israel? Have you condemned a daughter of Israel without an inquiry or a clear knowledge of the facts?
Now separate them far from one another for me, so that I may examine them.”

When they had been separated, Daniel said to the assembly, “Do not now look at the fact that these men are elders and say, ‘They certainly will not lie.’ I will question them according to what occurs to me.” He called one of them, and they brought the elder to the young man. Daniel said to him, “Listen, listen, you who have grown old in evil days! Now your sins have come upon you, the things you formerly did

when you were entrusted with hearing and judging cases that bring death: you condemned the innocent and would release the guilty, although the Lord says, ‘You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous.’
Now then, under what tree, and in what part of the garden, did you see them together?” The impious man said, “Under a mastic tree.”
The young man said, “You have indeed lied against your own soul, for the angel of the Lord will split your soul today.”
He moved this man aside and said to bring the other to him. To this man he said, “Why is your offspring corrupted, like Sidon’s and not like Judah’s? Beauty and filthy desire deceived you!
This is how you used to treat the daughters of Israel, and they were intimate with you because they were afraid. But a daughter of Judah did not endure bearing your disease in lawlessness.
Now then, tell me: under what tree, and in what part of the garden, did you catch them being intimate with one another?” He said, “Under a holm-oak.”
Daniel said, “Sinner, the angel of the Lord now stands holding his sword, until the people utterly destroy you both, so that he may saw you apart.”

The whole assembly cried out over the young man, because from their own mouths he had established that both were admittedly false witnesses. As the law prescribes, they did to them what they had wickedly plotted against their sister. They gagged them, took them out, and threw them into a ravine. Then the angel of the Lord cast fire through their midst. Innocent blood was saved that day.

For this reason the young are beloved of Jacob in their simplicity. Let us also be attentive to capable young sons, for the young will be devout, and a spirit of knowledge and understanding will be in them for ever and ever.
From the prophecy of Habakkuk, son of Joshua, of the tribe of Levi.
There was a certain priest named Daniel, son of Abal, a companion of the king of Babylon.
There was an idol, Bel, whom the Babylonians revered. Each day twelve artabas of fine flour, four sheep, and six metretas of oil were expended for him.
The king revered him and went each day to bow before him, but Daniel prayed to the Lord.
The king said to Daniel, “Why do you not bow before Bel?” Daniel said to the king, “I revere no one except the Lord God, who created heaven and earth and has lordship over all flesh.”
The king said to him, “Is this one, then, not a god? Do you not see how much is spent on him every day?”

Daniel said to him, “Certainly not! Let no one deceive you. This one is clay on the inside and bronze on the outside. I swear to you by the Lord, the God of gods, that this one has never eaten anything.”

The king became angry, called those in charge of the temple, and said to them, “Show who eats what is prepared for Bel. Otherwise, either you will die or Daniel, who claims that these things are not eaten by him.” They said, “Bel himself is the one who eats them.”

Daniel said to the king, “Let it be so. If I do not demonstrate that Bel is not the one who eats these things, I and all my people will die.” Bel had seventy priests, apart from their wives and children.
They brought the king into the idol-temple.

The food was set out before the king and Daniel. Mixed wine was brought in and placed before Bel. Daniel said, “You yourself see that these things are laid out, O king. So seal the locks of the temple yourself when it has been closed.”
The proposal pleased the king.

Daniel ordered his people to put everyone out of the temple and sprinkle the whole temple with ashes, without anyone outside his own group knowing. Then he ordered the temple to be sealed with the king’s ring and the rings of certain distinguished priests. It was done that way.

The next day they came to the place. Meanwhile, Bel’s priests had entered through secret doors, eaten everything laid before Bel, and drunk all the wine. Daniel said, “Men who are priests, inspect your seals to see whether they remain. And you, O king, examine whether anything has turned out contrary to what you expected.” They found the seal as it had been, and removed the seal.
They opened the doors and saw that everything set out had been consumed and the tables were empty. The king rejoiced and said to Daniel, “Bel is great, and there is no deceit in him.”
Daniel laughed heartily and said to the king, “Come, see the priests’ deceit.” Daniel said, “O king, whose footprints are these?”
The king said, “Those of men, women, and children.”

He went to the house where the priests were staying and found Bel’s food and the wine. Daniel showed the king the secret doors through which the priests would enter and consume what was laid before Bel.
The king brought them out of Bel’s temple and handed them over to Daniel. He gave Daniel the expenditure allocated to Bel, and destroyed Bel.
There was a dragon in the same place, and the Babylonians revered it.
The king said to Daniel, “Will you say that this one is bronze too? Behold, it lives, eats, and drinks. Bow before it.”
Daniel said, “O king, give me authority, and I will kill the dragon without iron or a rod.”
The king consented and said to him, “It is granted to you.”

Daniel took thirty minas of pitch, together with fat and hair, boiled them together, made a cake, and threw it into the dragon’s mouth. It ate and burst apart. He showed it to the king, saying, “Are these not the things you revere, O king?”
All the people from the country gathered against Daniel and said, “The king has become a Jew! He has destroyed Bel and killed the dragon.”
The king saw that the crowd of the country had gathered against him. He called his companions and said, “I hand Daniel over to destruction.”

There was a pit in which seven lions were kept. Those who plotted against the king were handed over to them, and each day two bodies of people condemned to death were supplied to them. The crowds threw Daniel into that pit so that he would be devoured and would not even receive burial. Daniel was in the pit for six days.
On the sixth day, Habakkuk had bread crumbled in a trough with stew, and a jar of mixed wine. He was going into the field to the reapers.
An angel of the Lord spoke to Habakkuk, saying, “Thus says the Lord God to you: ‘Take the meal you have to Daniel in the lions’ pit in Babylon.’”
Habakkuk said, “Lord God, I have not seen Babylon, and I do not know where the pit is.”
The angel of the Lord took Habakkuk by the hair of his head and set him above the pit in Babylon.
Habakkuk said to Daniel, “Get up and eat the meal that the Lord God has sent you.”
Daniel said, “For the Lord God has remembered me, He who does not abandon those who love Him.”
Daniel ate. The angel of the Lord returned Habakkuk to the place from which he had taken him on that same day. And the Lord God remembered Daniel.
After these things the king went out mourning Daniel. He bent down into the pit and saw him sitting there.
The king cried aloud and said, “The Lord God is great, and there is no other besides Him.”
The king brought Daniel out of the pit. Before Daniel’s eyes he threw into the pit those responsible for his destruction, and they were devoured.
